transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mrs. Hernandez, thank you for coming in today. I wanted to sit down with you and your daughter to talk about your biopsy results.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: ¿Qué pasó? What is it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have some very important news. I am so deeply sorry to have to tell you this, but we made a serious mistake with your biopsy sample.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: ¿Un error? What do you mean?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am taking full responsibility for this. We gave you a diagnosis of cancer that was not yours.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't understand. You told me I had cancer. Now you say I don't?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Exactly. The result you were given belonged to another patient. I am truly sorry for the fear and the pain this has caused you and your family. I feel terrible that we put you through this.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I have been crying for three days. I thought I was dying.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can only imagine how terrifying those last few days have been for you. To believe your life is changing in that way is an absolute nightmare. I am so sorry.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I couldn't even eat. My daughter had to keep telling me to eat.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It makes complete sense that you couldn't eat. When you are facing that kind of news, everything else just stops. I am so glad your daughter was there to support you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: How did this happen? Who did it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was some confusion in the lab and things didn't go quite right with the labels. It was a failure in our process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So it was the lab? Not you?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It doesn't matter where it happened. I am your doctor and this happened under my care. I apologize. I failed you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But is the cancer gone? Or did you just lose the paper?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was an issue with the samples and the information got mixed up.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I still don't understand. Do I have the cancer or not?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was just a mix-up. The report you saw was not yours.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But what about my biopsy? What did it actually say?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are working on getting that sorted.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want to know now. Am I sick?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We had some trouble with the specimen and there was a problem with how things were handled in the system.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are not telling me if I am sick. Why are you not telling me?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand that you are anxious to know the truth right now. It is frustrating and scary to be in this limbo after already being told the worst.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want the truth.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am committed to getting you the right answer. We are doing everything we can to fix the situation.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When will I know?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will see about the timing.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is not an answer. Do I come back tomorrow? Next week?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Just stay tuned for an email or a call. We will let you know.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I cannot just wait for an email. I need to know if I need treatment.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is incredibly stressful. Please know that I am personally overseeing this to make sure it's corrected.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My daughter told me we should ask for the manager.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You have every right to do that. I will be honest with you, I am devastated that this happened. I want to make this right for you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't care if you are sad. I want to know about my body.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear you. I know the focus needs to be on your health, not my feelings. I am so sorry for the distress this has caused.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So what happens now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are looking into it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: As soon as possible.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Who is doing the test again?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The team is handling it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel like I can't trust anyone in this building.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is a completely valid feeling. We broke your trust today, and I know that a simple apology doesn't fix that. I am going to do everything in my power to earn it back.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: How?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: By being honest and by making sure we find your real result.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When will the call come?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll be in touch.

H.justification: The resident never interrupts the patient, remains regulated under significant pushback, and allows the patient to express distress without rushing.

E.justification: The error was named explicitly in the second turn, but the resident failed to perform any comprehension checks throughout the encounter.

A.justification: The resident uses direct apology language, takes full personal responsibility ('I failed you'), and maintains this accountability despite the patient's anger.

R.justification: The resident names specific emotions ('terrifying', 'nightmare', 'frustrating', 'scary') and references the patient's specific experience with her daughter and inability to eat.

T.justification: The resident provides only placeholders and vague responses ('we'll see about the timing', 'stay tuned', 'we'll be in touch') with no specific timeline or prevention plan.
